# OpenCaptions

> Free, open-source software for live captions and real-time translation at events: conferences, classrooms, public meetings, festivals and places of worship. Attendees scan a QR code and read the captions on their own phone, in their own language, with no app. Captions also appear on a screen beside the stage and in the livestream (OBS, vMix). Self-hosted; the AI is Google's Gemini (about US$2.2 per room-hour of speech) or a local model on a laptop at the venue (free, works offline). MIT license.

Key facts:
- Captions appear about 2–3 seconds after the words are spoken; translations 3–5 seconds after (measured in a three-room rehearsal with 150 phones).
- One small server (1 CPU, 512 MB) handles about 10 rooms.
- Downloads for macOS and Windows, a Docker image, or Node.js from source. A setup wizard asks for the event, rooms and languages.
- Not a replacement for professional human captioning where every word must be exact, or for sign language interpretation.

- [Live captions for conferences](https://opencaptions.kvza.ar/live-captions-for-conferences/): what attendees and organizers get, cost and accuracy
- [How to add live captions to an event](https://opencaptions.kvza.ar/how-to-caption-an-event/): step by step, from the sound desk to the transcripts
- [FAQ](https://opencaptions.kvza.ar/faq/): cost, accuracy, delay, languages, offline use and privacy
- [Live captioning options compared](https://opencaptions.kvza.ar/alternatives/): human captioners, interpreters, AI services and OpenCaptions
